questions.q1_polya_budget10_reachability: user: can we raise edit budget 5->10 and test?
questions.q2_budget_perf_effect: user: have we measured edit budget effect on model performance?

polyA_measured_neighborhood.note: polyA task needs >=6-8 edits to cover majority; budget-5 is algebraically dead (9.9%)

combination_space.note: naive sampling hit-probability at B=10 collapses ~1e-9 fold vs B=5; budget raise alone does NOT restore support - needs directional sampling

e8a_budget_reachability.budget_hard_coded: edit_budgets=(1,3,5) is protocol-level _require assertion in build_route2_generation_eligibility_v1.py + v332 matrix; changing to 10 requires amendment + source change + training-data re-evaluation

e8b_budget_vs_performance.finding: polyA: rho INCREASES with edit count (4-5: 0.44-0.60 -> 6-8: 0.71 -> 9-12: 0.74-0.84) - multi-edit rewrites are MORE predictable, not less. MRL: rho rises 1->3 edits (signal concentration). Budget affects coverage (algebraic) more than model quality (rho per stratum stable/rising).

answer_synthesis.budget10_test: RECOMMENDED but NOT naive-sampling: reachability 9.9%->89.2% justifies the test, but combination space explodes 1e-9x hit-rate -> must pair budget raise with neighborhood-directed sampling (D15) or genscore top-K explore-select (V6.5 mechanism). Requires: amendment (protocol _require), eligibility rebuild, budget-sweep arm design.
answer_synthesis.budget_perf_effect: first stratified measurement done this session (E8b); no prior budget sweep existed. Per-stratum rho is stable-to-rising with edit count, so budget is a COVERAGE lever not a QUALITY lever for critic.
